items.label: f02-stable-not-idempotent
items.front: Why is a repeat DONE save not "idempotent", even though completedAt no longer changes?
items.back: Each request still bumps Task.updatedAt (Prisma @updatedAt) and inserts a new task.updated audit row. Say precisely which field is stable rather than calling the whole endpoint idempotent from one assertion.

items.label: f04-what-tests-miss
items.front: What does the focused completion test suite NOT prove?
items.back: Decorators are stripped and DTO, Prisma and audit are stubs, so it proves nothing about HTTP validation, dependency injection, authentication or SQL. The e2e file covers only health, so no automated test sends a real PATCH /api/tasks/:id.

items.label: f03-do-not-tidy
items.front: Why should you not change dto.status ? ... to dto.status !== undefined ? ... while fixing completedAt?
items.back: @IsOptional() lets null through, so { "status": null } currently skips the branch. A presence check would pass status: null for a required enum, which Prisma rejects as a 500. Leave unrelated conditions alone until the new contract is decided and tested.

items.label: f01-four-cases
items.front: What are the four status cases TasksService.update distinguishes for completedAt?
items.back: Entering DONE from another status: new Date(). Repeating DONE: keep the existing value. Leaving DONE (any other status): null. Omitting status: neither status nor completedAt is in the payload; absent is different from null, which would erase history.

items.prompt: Writer A reads an OPEN task at line 52 and pauses. Writer B then completes it with { "status": "DONE" } at time T1. A resumes and also sends DONE, saving at time T2. What completedAt is stored at the end?

choices.text: T1, because Prisma rejects A's stale update
T1, since the second DONE is treated as a repeat
null, as two DONE writes cancel each other out
T2, because A decides from its stale OPEN read

choices: T1, because Prisma rejects A's stale update
T1, since the second DONE is treated as a repeat
null, as two DONE writes cancel each other out
T2, because A decides from its stale OPEN read

items.explanation: A's before still says OPEN, so it takes the "entering DONE" path and writes new Date() (T2). The update has only where: { id } and no version check, so nothing detects the race.

items.prompt: Someone "fixes" the bug by always writing before.completedAt whenever status is DONE. Which test catches it, and how?

choices.text: Test 1, since a repeat DONE now writes the fixed clock time instead
Test 3, because data gains a completedAt key
None of them, since all three still pass
Test 2: IN_PROGRESS to DONE writes null, so getTime() throws

choices: Test 1, since a repeat DONE now writes the fixed clock time instead
Test 3, because data gains a completedAt key
None of them, since all three still pass
Test 2: IN_PROGRESS to DONE writes null, so getTime() throws

items.explanation: Test 2 moves a task from IN_PROGRESS (completedAt null) to DONE and expects the fixed clock instant. Reusing before.completedAt writes null, and calling getTime() on it throws.

items.prompt: prisma.task.update succeeds, but the following audit.log insert throws. What state is the task left in?

choices.text: Both are rolled back by the surrounding transaction
The task change stays committed without its audit row
The task change is undone by a compensating update
The task update is retried until the audit succeeds

choices: Both are rolled back by the surrounding transaction
The task change stays committed without its audit row
The task change is undone by a compensating update
The task update is retried until the audit succeeds

items.explanation: The audit write is a separate awaited call after the update, not inside prisma.$transaction. Once the update has committed, an audit failure cannot undo it.

choices.text: null, as completedAt is reset on each save
Monday 09:00, the value it already had
No completedAt key, since status is unchanged
Tuesday's save time, a fresh new Date()

choices: null, as completedAt is reset on each save
Monday 09:00, the value it already had
No completedAt key, since status is unchanged
Tuesday's save time, a fresh new Date()

items.explanation: With dto.status DONE and before.status DONE, the inner ternary selects before.completedAt, so the Monday value is written back. Writing new Date() was the original bug.

The row's updatedAt time

items.prompt: In the vm-loaded test, assert.deepEqual(data, { priority: "HIGH" }) fails even though data holds exactly that. Why does test 3 compare Object.keys(data) instead?

choices.text: data is a Prisma proxy object, so deepEqual cannot read its keys
Objects made in the vm context have a different Object.prototype
The audit double mutates data after update has recorded it
deepEqual compares Date fields by reference rather than by value

choices: data is a Prisma proxy object, so deepEqual cannot read its keys
Objects made in the vm context have a different Object.prototype
The audit double mutates data after update has recorded it
deepEqual compares Date fields by reference rather than by value

items.explanation: The service runs in a separate vm realm, so its objects carry that realm's prototype, and deepEqual reports "same structure but not reference-equal". Arrays from Object.keys are built in the test's realm.

items.prompt: A client sends { "status": null } for a DONE task. What happens, given that @IsOptional() lets null through validation?

choices.text: A 400, as the DTO rejects null for its status enum field
Prisma rejects status: null, and the request then fails with a 500 error
The task becomes OPEN, and completedAt is cleared to a null
The status branch is skipped; no status or completedAt is written

choices: A 400, as the DTO rejects null for its status enum field
Prisma rejects status: null, and the request then fails with a 500 error
The task becomes OPEN, and completedAt is cleared to a null
The status branch is skipped; no status or completedAt is written

items.explanation: null is falsy, so dto.status ? ... : {} contributes nothing. The guide warns that "tidying" the check to !== undefined would instead pass status: null to Prisma and produce a 500.
